newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NYMEX mulls expansion of copper delivery system.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX mulls expansion of copper delivery system.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) is in the process of exploring the possibility of allowing warehouses outside the U.S. to be utilised in its copper contract's delivery system, an official said on Monday.

Erik Bucht, an international commodity analyst with the research department of NYMEX, said at a conference in Singapore that the exchange is seeking to extend North American price discovery to the rest of the world.
"Chile is one potential, but we are also considering delivery points for our copper contract in other places around the Pacific rim," he said.
Bucht said another matter under study is "region-specific futures contracts for other metals that would be traded on NYMEX-ACCESS and cash settled."

The NYMEX-ACCESS terminal is the after-hours electronic trading system which allows dealers in the Hong Kong Futures Exchange (HKFE) and the Sydney Futures Exchange to trade in NYMEX futures contracts for gold, silver, natural gas and other commodities.
"If that occurred, it would be a major departure for the exchange because all NYMEX and COMEX division physical commodity contracts, metals and energy, provide for physical delivery," Bucht said.
